page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processors, the instance allocates 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with dual-thread hyperthreading. The configuration is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not bundled, necessitating network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations. Hardware accelerators and GPUs are not present.

Benchmark assessments locate this server primarily in the mid-tier performance spectrum. Multi-core compute performance yields 14,822.17 in stress-ng and 8,666.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing, whereas stress-ng single-core throughput places in the lower quartile at 1,408.79. Memory subsystems exhibit 96.6 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth alongside 55.45 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth, rising to 818.42 GB/sec for small-block cached read cycles. Transactional performance reaches 14.1 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks and 5,733.5 in PassMark database execution. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI.

The qualitative profile of this server favors configurations that require elevated memory allocation per processing thread without over-provisioning compute resources. Tradeoffs include reliance on external disk volumes for I/O and moderate per-core performance. The hardware configuration aligns with data-intensive tasks such as in-memory data caching, transactional databases, extract-transform-load (ETL) processing, and mid-sized web serving environments.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-16 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores on 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processors alongside 128 GB of system RAM. Its high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU provides substantial memory density for operational datasets without requiring additional compute scaling. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate mid-tier results across standard metrics, including an 8,666.0 Geekbench multi-core score, 96.6 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth, and 14.1 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Supported CPU vector capabilities include AVX-512 and VNNI. The instance profile is suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, relational databases, ETL batch pipelines, and backend application hosting.
